title: Media agents — check what stuck
intro: Eight self-check questions written from the course notes (this course has no official graded quiz).

choices: Predicting the next token sequentially
Starting from noise and refining the whole output pass by pass, in latent space
Copying the nearest training image
Sampling a random image and cropping it
questions.explanation: Diffusion = iterative denoising of the whole output (condition → denoise → decode) — the sculptor mental model. Sequential next-token prediction is the autoregressive paradigm.

choices: Instruction following, compositional accuracy, and fine control
High-fidelity texture and detail
Running without any compute
Producing audio only
questions.explanation: AR builds sequentially like an LLM — its strength is control. Diffusion owns fidelity and texture. Hybrids chain AR structure into diffusion detail.

questions.prompt: Why hand your prompt keywords to an LLM before generating?
choices: To count the tokens
The image model prefers one rich descriptive paragraph — the LLM weaves the keywords into it
Because keyword lists are forbidden by the API
To translate the prompt into English
questions.explanation: LLM-enhanced prompting: keywords structure your thinking, but the generation model's deep language understanding favors a detailed paragraph — so an LLM acts as the director.

questions.prompt: In the video prompt formula, which dimensions exist that images don't need?
choices: Subject and style
Temporal pacing, camera movement, and audio
Lighting and composition
Aspect ratio
questions.explanation: Video adds the time dimensions: how the scene changes (temporal), motion of the frame itself (pan/tilt), and native audio (dialogue, sound effects).

choices: The final safety review before shipping
A fast, deterministic first filter — one alignment score to discard clear failures
A tool that explains why an image failed
A video-editing model
questions.explanation: SigLIP's dual encoder gives one 0→1 similarity, cheap and deterministic — ideal at the funnel's mouth. It can't tell you why something failed (that's the judge/rubric tier) and it isn't a human sign-off.

choices: Averaging pixel differences against a reference image
Decomposing the prompt into questions, then verifying each against the image — per-element pass/fail
Asking three humans to vote
Measuring generation latency
questions.explanation: Decompose → verify: the same question set applied to every candidate makes comparisons fair, and per-element results are interpretable — you know WHICH part failed.

questions.prompt: The video agent's evaluator returns failure_type: "audio". The right retry is…
choices: Regenerate both the reference image and the video
Regenerate the video only, reusing the reference image
Re-plan every scene from scratch
Lower the pass threshold
questions.explanation: Targeted retries: audio failure → the frame was fine, regenerate only the Veo clip. Visual failure → regenerate both. Classifying the failure is what keeps retries cheap.

questions.prompt: In the ADK triple, the 'instruction' is…
choices: The system prompt that sets how the agent orchestrates its tools
The Python function the agent calls
The model's weights
A billing configuration
questions.explanation: Model = the brain choosing the next tool; tools = the capabilities; instruction = the SYSTEM_PROMPT encoding the loop (analyse → generate → evaluate → retry with feedback, capped).
